summary.headline: Bandhan Bank cut its FY27 exit ROA aspiration to 1.2%-1.4% from 1.6%-1.8%, citing funding costs and tech costs; Q1 PAT rose 35% YoY to INR 502 crores.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 showed better seasonal resilience than prior first quarters: gross advances grew 16% YoY to INR 1.56 lakh crores, with non-EEB up 27% and secured book at 57% of advances. Deposits grew 7% YoY to INR 1.65 lakh crores as the bank deliberately cut bulk deposits 13% YoY, while CASA rose 16% YoY to INR 48,479 crores. Margin held at 6.2%, PAT was INR 502 crores (+35% YoY), and gross NPA eased to 3.1%. Management lowered its Q4 FY27 exit ROA guidance to 1.2%-1.4% from 1.6%-1.8%, attributing the cut to external factors (funding costs, technology costs, Middle East energy crisis, monsoon), and said the medium-term aspiration could slip beyond its original timeline.

financial_highlights.change: down from 32% a year ago; bulk deposits -13% YoY
broadly stable vs Q4 FY26 (5.8% in Q2, 5.9% in Q3 FY26)

financial_highlights.value: INR 2,166 crores (includes INR 61 crores one-time gratuity)

financial_highlights.change: down from 2.0% in Q4 FY26; EEB credit cost 3.3%
PCR 71.1% reported, 74.3% incl. security receipt provisions; 86% incl. technical write-offs per CEO
vs INR 1,028 crores in Q4 FY26; EEB from INR 690 crores
Q1 FY26 included ~INR 250 crores treasury gains; ex-treasury non-interest income +22% YoY; third-party distribution income +47% YoY

segments.name: EEB (microfinance)
segments.commentary: EEB book INR 52,641 crores, flat YoY; Q1 seasonal decline smaller than prior years. Collection efficiency ex-NPA 98.5% in June vs 98.6% in March; 0-90 DPD pool rose to 3.5% from 3.1%, attributed to April holidays and West Bengal elections. No yield hike in Q1; last hike was 100 bps in February 2026.

segments.name: Non-EEB / secured
segments.commentary: Non-EEB grew 27% YoY and is two-thirds of the book; secured book +27% YoY to 57% of advances. Retail assets +45% YoY (CV/CE, auto, gold loans), though gold loan sourcing was disrupted April to mid-May by a new RBI circular. Wholesale banking +38% YoY to 33% of advances.

segments.name: Housing finance
segments.commentary: Housing finance is 22% of advances. Mortgage book slightly declined QoQ during restructuring into three verticals; INR 291 crores of housing NPAs sold to an ARC, with about INR 120 crores of cash recovery.

segments.name: Retail deposits
segments.commentary: Retail deposits (CASA plus retail term deposits) grew 16% YoY and are 74% of total deposits; retail deposits grew over 15% YoY per CEO.

guidance_outlook: Exit Q4 FY27 ROA revised to 1.2%-1.4% (from 1.6%-1.8%), described as probable on current visibility; medium-term 1.6%-1.8% aspiration unchanged but timeline may extend.

NIM: earlier line of sight to 6.5% by Q4 FY27 is withdrawn; management expects the 6.2% margin to be hard to hold, with moderate pressure from higher deposit and cost of funds. Savings bank cost of funds up about 20-25 bps.
Opex-to-assets guided at around 4.2% but running at 4.3% in Q1; expected to remain elevated. Tech cost ~8% of total cost (~9.5% incl. depreciation), to be kept within 10% and tapered to 8% over time.
Credit cost guidance of 1.6%-1.8% unchanged; management expects a slight further improvement.
Other income expected to add 10-20 bps to ROA over the year.
FY27 advance growth guidance of 14% (EEB 5-10%, non-EEB 20%+) maintained; EEB to rise to 33-34% of book (up to 35% cap), and secured mix target 60%.
capex_capacity: Tech spend remains elevated: focus on LOS, CRS, DCDR and automated DR; management says investment years continue to FY28, with productivity gains expected in about 18 months.
Branch channel activation: about INR 900 crores of assets sourced via branches in Q4 FY26 vs INR 200 crores per month earlier; plan to reduce DSA dependence.
Four to five digital products launched or in progress (Legacy, Elite, Elite+, revamped corporate salary packages); credit card launch pending.
Forex and cash management products added in wholesale banking in the last quarter.
Bank has 4,400 business units (BUs) and plans to make metro and urban BUs sales points.
demand_pricing: Microfinance: no yield hike in Q1 FY27; last 100 bps hike in February 2026. Management says it is growing EEB cautiously, and competitive deposit rates are pressuring funding costs.
Liquidity: CD ratio 94% with LCR 140%; FCNRB mobilised INR 30 crores in the quarter.
Corporate: corporate book grew about 38%; wholesale margins are dilutive, which management justified as a route to fee and other income.
Retail: growth slowed to single digit overall per CEO; ex the OD-against-term-deposit product, retail grew about 5% QoQ.
Energy crisis and monsoon risk are seen as the main threats to microfinance borrowers' collections and credit costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the ROA aspiration cut, and is it due to asset quality or funding costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cut is due to external factors: NIM stretch of about 30 bps (funding costs, no further margin uplift to 6.5%) and about 10 bps opex (tech costs ~4.3% of assets vs 4.2% guided). Credit cost is improving (2.0% to 1.8%).

qa_highlights.question: Why hasn't FCNR and easing liquidity relieved funding costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said liquidity remains tight (about INR 2.5 lakh crore need vs INR 1 lakh crore available) and larger banks are raising deposit rates; the benefit of repo cuts was used up in Q1 and savings bank costs are up 20-25 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Have microfinance yields been raised?
qa_highlights.answer: No hike in Q1 FY27. A 100 bps hike was taken in February 2026 (Q4 FY26), and management says there are no plans for another for now.

qa_highlights.question: Why did retail and mortgage growth slow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited cautious growth, the housing vertical restructuring, and the run-off of the OD-against-term-deposit product. Ex that product, retail grew about 5% QoQ; gold loans were hit by the new RBI circular in April to mid-May.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the bank growing low-margin wholesale banking?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wholesale is an entry point for wallet share and fee income (LCs, forex, cash management). Pricing is said to be comparable to or better than the industry, and the aim is to offset NII pressure with other income.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-to-income and opex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost-to-income (about 62%) will stay flat for about a year and taper from FY28. Opex-to-assets is expected to stay near 4.3% and then fall once tech investments are complete.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the collection efficiency for June look lower than the quarter average?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the quarter figure includes recoveries of in-quarter slippages, which the single-month figure excludes, so the gap is technical.

risks_watch: Funding cost pressure: savings bank cost of funds up 20-25 bps; NIM may fall from 6.2%.
Tech cost inflation from supply chain and chip constraints; opex-to-assets 4.3% vs 4.2% guided.
EEB early delinquency (0-90 DPD) at 3.5% vs 3.1% in Q4; energy crisis and monsoon may hit microfinance collections.
Gold loan sourcing disruption from the new RBI circular; Q2 retail growth expected to recover.
Whether ARC-related recoveries (about INR 120 crores) are one-off; the recovery pace is being watched.
Dependence on DSAs; cost-to-income around 62% with branch-led sourcing still early.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious on the outlook: management openly cut the ROA guidance and attributed it to external factors, while stressing that internal execution, credit cost and asset quality are on track. Answers were sometimes vague on the mechanics of the margin and opex trade-offs, and some questions had to be repeated.
key_quotes: The revise guidance on RoA is on account of the external factors and no internal factors, I would say, has any impact on revising the guidance.
Based on this visibility available, we believe an ROA in the range of 1.2% to 1.4% of the exit of Q4FY27 would be probable.
So the NIM, what we had expected earlier may get somewhat of impact because of the rising cost of funds for that year.
Gross NPA at 3.1%, net NPA at 0.9% and provision coverage at 86%, including the technical write-offs.
Consequently, we think that the realization of this aspiration could extend beyond the time line we had originally envisaged.
So the question is that we may not expect delinquency, but at the same time, we cannot be over aggressive.

adds.what: 4,400 business units (BUs) in network; plan to convert metro and urban BUs into sales points
Branch channel activation: ~INR 900 crores assets sourced via branches in Q4 FY26 vs INR 200 crores per month earlier

growth.why: Advance growth guidance of 14% for FY27 held (EEB 5-10%, non-EEB 20%+), with Q1 gross advances +16% YoY and non-EEB +27%; but the Q4 FY27 exit ROA was cut to 1.2-1.4% from 1.6-1.8%, NIM 6.5% target withdrawn, and opex/assets running 4.3% vs 4.2% guide, with backing mainly from demand in non-EEB, wholesale and branch sourcing rather than specific capacity.
